mechanism: AR-14034 SR is an investigational sustained-release intravitreal implant designed to deliver axitinib, a small-molecule pan-VEGF receptor inhibitor that inhibits signaling through known VEGF receptors and is intended to reduce choroidal neovascularization and vascular leakage.
development_status: ClinicalTrials.gov lists NOVA-1 (NCT05769153) as an active, not recruiting Phase 1/2 two-stage study in neovascular age-related macular degeneration. Stage 1 included an open-label lower-dose cohort receiving one aflibercept 2 mg injection at Week -1 and one AR-14034 SR lower-dose intravitreal insertion at baseline, with up to one AR-14034 SR retreatment between Weeks 4 and 36 based on disease activity. Stage 2 randomizes participants to one or two AR-14034 SR insertions versus labeled aflibercept. Actual enrollment is 139, estimated primary completion is May 2027, estimated study completion is October 2027, and no ClinicalTrials.gov results are posted.
clinical_summary: The lower-dose assignment maps to the Stage 1 dose-escalation cohort, not a disclosed pivotal dose. AR-14034 SR's potential differentiation is durability and broader VEGF-receptor blockade: Aerie described axitinib as inhibiting all known VEGF receptors and preclinical data as supporting up to 12 months of retinal drug exposure after a single intravitreal injection. The current human study has no posted results; Stage 2's primary efficacy endpoint is mean change from baseline in ETDRS best corrected visual acuity averaged across Weeks 44 and 48, with CST and BCVA through Week 56 as secondary measures. Current differentiation remains modest because the evidence is early and wet AMD already has durable anti-VEGF options including Eylea HD, Vabysmo, and Susvimo.
safety_summary: No AR-14034 SR human safety results are posted on ClinicalTrials.gov. Relevant risks are inferred from the intravitreal implant/injection route and anti-VEGF class analogs: Eylea labeling warns that endophthalmitis, retinal detachments, retinal vasculitis, intraocular pressure increases, and arterial thromboembolic events may occur after intravitreal VEGF inhibition; Susvimo's ocular implant label highlights implant/procedure risks including endophthalmitis, retinal detachment, implant dislocation, vitreous hemorrhage, conjunctival erosion/retraction, and postoperative intraocular inflammation. AR-14034's bioerodible implant design may avoid refill-port mechanics, but procedure-related and local ocular safety remain key evidence gaps until NOVA-1 reports.
management_tools: Confirm FDA-approved nAMD indication, dosing interval, and eye-specific eligibility before coverage
Require diagnosis of active choroidal neovascularization secondary to AMD and baseline BCVA/OCT documentation
Require retina specialist prescribing or administration
Define continuation criteria based on maintained or improved BCVA, reduced central subfield thickness, absence of unacceptable ocular toxicity, and retreatment need
Set dose and frequency limits aligned to final label, including whether repeat AR-14034 SR insertion is permitted within 12 months
Avoid concurrent routine use with another intravitreal anti-VEGF agent except label-supported rescue or supplemental therapy
Consider preferred-product or step-through positioning versus lower-cost bevacizumab, aflibercept biosimilars, Eylea/Eylea HD, Vabysmo, or Susvimo depending on final efficacy and durability
evidence_gaps: ClinicalTrials.gov has no posted results for NCT05769153.
The lower-dose milligram strength is not disclosed in the public ClinicalTrials.gov intervention description.
The lower-dose arm is a Stage 1 dose-escalation cohort; Stage 2 uses one- and two-insertion AR-14034 SR arms rather than explicitly named lower-dose and higher-dose arms.
No public AR-14034 SR Phase 2 efficacy, safety, durability, regulatory filing plan, or commercial price was found.
Annual cost uses wet AMD anti-VEGF and sustained-delivery analogs because AR-14034 SR has no disclosed commercial price.
Final utilization management will depend on whether AR-14034 SR is positioned for treatment-naive patients, previously treated/responding patients, or high-burden patients needing durable therapy.

sources.title: Study of AR-14034 in Participants With Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration (nAMD)
supports: NOVA-1 is a Phase 1/2 two-stage study of AR-14034 Sustained Release implant compared with intravitreal anti-VEGF treatment in nAMD.
Sponsor is Alcon Research; other study ID is RTE888-E001.
Overall status is active, not recruiting; actual start was 2023-12-06; actual enrollment is 139; estimated primary completion is 2027-05; estimated study completion is 2027-10.
Stage 1 is a 48-week open-label dose-escalation evaluation of two AR-14034 SR dose levels.
Cohort 1 receives aflibercept 2 mg at Week -1 and AR-14034 SR lower-dose intravitreal insertion at baseline, with up to one retreatment between Weeks 4 and 36 based on disease activity.
Stage 2 is a 56-week double-masked randomized active-comparator study of one or two AR-14034 SR insertions versus labeled aflibercept, followed by a 16-week open-label extension.
Primary endpoint is mean change from baseline in ETDRS BCVA averaged across Weeks 44 and 48 in Stage 2; secondary endpoints include BCVA by visit and CST by visit through Week 56.
ClinicalTrials.gov hasResults is false.

sources.title: Aerie Pharmaceuticals 2021 Form 10-K: AR-14034 SR Implant
supports: Aerie described AR-14034 SR as a sustained-release implant designed to deliver axitinib, a small-molecule kinase inhibitor of VEGF receptors.
Aerie described axitinib as inhibiting signaling from all four VEGFs by inhibiting all known VEGF receptors.
Preclinical data showed inhibition of choroidal neovascularization and reduced vessel leakage in wet AMD and DME models.

Axitinib was formulated with a proprietary polymer blend to produce an injectable bioerodible implant with potential to sustain retinal drug concentrations for up to 12 months after one intravitreal injection.
Aerie stated AR-14034 SR could potentially provide once-yearly injection treatment for wet AMD, DME, and related retinal diseases.

sources.title: Aerie Pharmaceuticals Axitinib Implant (AR-14034) Overview
supports: Aerie characterized axitinib as a pan-VEGF receptor inhibitor and AR-14034 as a development-stage product candidate not approved by any regulatory agency.
Investor presentation stated preclinical release data supported a target duration of up to 12 months in clinic.
Investor presentation stated IND filing was planned for the second half of 2022.

sources.title: DailyMed: EYLEA (aflibercept) injection, solution
supports: Eylea is indicated for neovascular wet age-related macular degeneration.
Recommended nAMD dosing is 2 mg intravitreal injection every 4 weeks for the first 3 months, then 2 mg once every 8 weeks.
Label warnings include endophthalmitis, retinal detachments, retinal vasculitis with or without occlusion, intraocular pressure increases, and potential arterial thromboembolic events.
Common adverse reactions include conjunctival hemorrhage, eye pain, cataract, vitreous detachment, vitreous floaters, and increased intraocular pressure.

sources.title: DailyMed: EYLEA HD (aflibercept) injection, solution
supports: Eylea HD is indicated for neovascular wet age-related macular degeneration.
Recommended nAMD dosing is 8 mg intravitreal injection every 4 weeks for the first three doses, then 8 mg every 8 to 16 weeks.
PULSAR compared Eylea HD every 12 or 16 weeks after three initial monthly doses with Eylea 2 mg every 8 weeks after three initial monthly doses.

sources.title: DailyMed: SUSVIMO (ranibizumab injection), for intravitreal use via ocular implant
supports: Susvimo is indicated for nAMD patients who previously responded to at least two intravitreal VEGF inhibitor injections.
Recommended nAMD dose is 2 mg continuously delivered via ocular implant with refills every 24 weeks.
Label carries a boxed warning for endophthalmitis and states the implant had up to a three-fold higher rate of endophthalmitis than monthly intravitreal ranibizumab.

Implant and procedure risks include rhegmatogenous retinal detachment, implant dislocation, vitreous hemorrhage, conjunctival erosion or retraction, conjunctival bleb, postoperative visual acuity decrease, and postoperative intraocular inflammation.

sources.title: CMS April 2026 Medicare Part B Payment Limit Files
supports: April 2026 ASP file lists J0178 aflibercept injection at $731.885 per 1 mg.
April 2026 ASP file lists J0177 aflibercept HD injection at $301.177 per 1 mg.
April 2026 ASP file lists J2777 faricimab-svoa at $32.866 per 0.1 mg.
CMS states ASP pricing files do not determine coverage and local MACs may process Part B claims when reasonable and necessary.

sources.title: SUSVIMO Ocular Implantation Cartons Ordering Guide
supports: Susvimo implant with insertion tool carton list price is $950.
Susvimo ranibizumab vial and initial fill needle carton WAC is $8,000.
Both cartons must be procured to perform the implantation procedure and additional discounts may be available.

sources.title: Aetna Clinical Policy Bulletin 0701: Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor Inhibitors for Ocular Indications
supports: Aetna policy requires precertification for ophthalmologic VEGF inhibitors including aflibercept, aflibercept HD, faricimab, ranibizumab, and Susvimo in applicable commercial plan designs.
Aflibercept and aflibercept HD are medically necessary for neovascular wet AMD when criteria are met.

Continuation of aflibercept therapy requires positive clinical response such as improvement or maintenance in BCVA or visual field, or reduced rate of vision decline or risk of more severe vision loss.

Policy states Aetna commercial plans may require a trial of a lower-cost preferred drug expected to produce equivalent therapeutic results before approving a higher-cost drug within the same therapeutic class.

expected_launch_window.method: Derived from active Phase 1/2 status, estimated primary completion in May 2027, estimated study completion in October 2027, absence of posted human results, and the likely need for at least one pivotal wet AMD program plus regulatory review.
expected_launch_window.explanation: A launch before 2031 is unlikely unless the Phase 1/2 study produces unusually registrational evidence or Alcon accelerates directly into a rapid pivotal program after 2027.

annual_cost_range.method: Low estimate uses Eylea HD ASP as a durable anti-VEGF analog at five 8 mg injections in year 1: $301.177 x 8 mg x 5 = $12,047. High estimate uses Susvimo sustained-delivery analog first-year list cost: $950 implant + two $8,000 ranibizumab cartons = $16,950.
annual_cost_range.explanation: AR-14034 SR has no disclosed price. The range anchors to current nAMD durable anti-VEGF drug acquisition and sustained-delivery implant analogs, excluding administration, surgery/procedure fees, imaging, office visits, adverse-event management, rebates, discounts, and supplemental rescue injections.

clinical_differentiation.method: Balanced potential once-yearly bioerodible pan-VEGF receptor implant profile against no posted human efficacy/safety data, the lower-dose arm's Stage 1-only status, and existing durable nAMD competitors.
clinical_differentiation.explanation: Durability could be meaningful if confirmed, but current evidence is preclinical plus an ongoing Phase 1/2 trial, and established anti-VEGF products already offer extended intervals or sustained delivery.

budget_impact.method: Assessed large nAMD eligible population, medical-benefit administration, analog annual drug cost around $12k-$17k, possible procedure costs, and offsetting potential for fewer injections if durability is confirmed.
budget_impact.explanation: Per-patient drug cost is likely material and utilization could be broad, but payer controls and ophthalmic anti-VEGF management pathways already exist.

disruption_risk.method: Rated from early development stage, possible once-yearly implant differentiation, procedure/retreatment uncertainty, and mature competitive/payer infrastructure in wet AMD.
disruption_risk.explanation: AR-14034 SR could alter visit and injection burden if durable, but the near-term risk is limited by lack of results and likely need for pivotal development.

recommended_action.method: Recommended action reflects Phase 1/2 status, no posted results, undisclosed dose and price, but potentially meaningful durability if the program advances.
recommended_action.explanation: Monitor NOVA-1 results, dose selection, and pivotal-trial plans before drafting product-specific policy; retain general anti-VEGF/implant management concepts for launch readiness.

quality_flags: Assigned asset name includes 'lower dose,' but ClinicalTrials.gov does not disclose the lower-dose strength.
The lower-dose intervention appears only in Stage 1 Cohort 1; Stage 2 uses AR-14034 SR one-injection and two-injection arms, so the lower dose may not represent the final selected regimen.
No ClinicalTrials.gov results are posted for NCT05769153.
AR-14034 SR is investigational and has no disclosed commercial price; annual cost is analog-derived.
Ownership/source lineage note: AR-14034 came from Aerie's pipeline, and Alcon completed acquisition of Aerie in November 2022; current ClinicalTrials.gov sponsor is Alcon Research.
Safety assessment is route/class/implant-analog based until AR-14034 SR human ocular safety data are publicly reported.
